# Vienna 1683 – Energy & engines

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Animal-powered machines (horse gin, treadwheel)** [`animal_power_gin`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/animal_power_gin.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Once the Danube and Wien river mills are lost to the besiegers, horse and hand mills inside the walls must grind the city's grain. Local: horse whims (Göpel) at the Schemnitz mines.
- **Water wheel** [`water_wheel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_wheel.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Ship mills moored in the Danube arms and mills on the Wien river grind for the city; all lie outside the walls. Alpine valleys drive hammers and saws. Local: Danube ship mills; mills on the Wien river; Styrian and Lower Austrian hammer works.
- **Windmill** [`windmill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/windmill.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Known, but water is cheap here and windmills are few. Leibniz is at this moment trying to pump the Harz mines with windmills, against the miners' resistance. Elsewhere: Holland: drainage and sawing mills; Harz (Clausthal): Leibniz's windmill pumps, 1680–1685.
- **Water turbine** [`water_turbine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_turbine.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Small horizontal-wheel mills turn in Alpine brooks. Nobody thinks of an enclosed wheel running full of water under pressure, and nobody can calculate one. Local: horizontal 'Stock' or 'Floder' mills in Alpine valleys.
- **Crank, connecting rod and flywheel** [`crank_connecting_rod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crank_connecting_rod.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high
- **Piston pumps (suction and force pump)** [`piston_pump`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/piston_pump.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. Mine pumps in tiers worked by water-wheel rod engines, well pumps and fire syringes. Barrels are bored wood or cast bronze. The fire hose is a new Dutch invention. Local: Schemnitz and Idrija mine pumps; city fire syringes; arsenal founders. Elsewhere: Amsterdam: Jan van der Heyden's fire engine with hoses (1672); Nuremberg: Hans Hautsch's fire engine; Marly: the great Seine pumping machine, building 1681–1684.
- **Hydraulic ram** [`hydraulic_ram`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydraulic_ram.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Unknown. Bronze founders and plumbers of lead and wooden pipes can make one; the valves must stand constant hammering. Local: bronze founders; well and pipe masters (Brunnenmeister).
- **Charcoal burning** [`charcoal_burning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/charcoal_burning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: charcoal burners of the Wienerwald.
- **Deep coal mining (drainage, ventilation, safety lamp)** [`coal_mining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coal_mining.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept low. Wood and charcoal heat the city and the ironworks; mineral coal is neither dug nor wanted here, and its smoke is thought unhealthy. Elsewhere: Liège and Newcastle coalfields; London burns sea coal.
- **Coal gas lighting** [`gas_lighting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gas_lighting.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium
- **Argand lamp (hollow wick and glass chimney)** [`argand_lamp`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/argand_lamp.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Light comes from tallow candles, wax for the rich, and flat-wick oil lamps; the streets are unlit. Brass workers and glassmakers can make the hollow wick and chimney. Local: brass workers (Gürtler); glassmakers.
- **Drilling for brine, gas and oil** [`oil_drilling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oil_drilling.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. Rock oil skimmed from seeps is an apothecary's remedy. Deep boring is unknown; brine comes from mined salt (Hallstatt, Hallein), not from drilled wells. Local: apothecaries (petroleum as medicine).
- **Steam reaction toy (aeolipile)** [`steam_aeolipile`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/steam_aeolipile.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Hero's ball and Branca's steam jet on a wheel are stock items in Kircher and Schott; copper fire-blowers exist. It is a cabinet toy, not a source of work. Local: coppersmiths; Jesuit physics lessons.
- **Boilers and the safety valve** [`safety_valve_boiler`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/safety_valve_boiler.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Papin's 'digester' with weighted safety valve (London 1679, printed 1681) is a rumour from the journals. Gun founders can cast the vessel; sealing lid and valve seat is the work. Local: bronze and gun founders; coppersmiths. Elsewhere: Venice: Denis Papin, 1681–1684; London: Royal Society.
- **Pistonless steam pump (Savery)** [`savery_steam_pump`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/savery_steam_pump.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. Books show steam pushing water from a vessel (della Porta, de Caus). No working engine exists anywhere. Soldered copper vessels burst; deep mines would be the customer. Local: Schemnitz mine administration; coppersmiths.
- **Atmospheric steam engine (Newcomen type)** [`atmospheric_engine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atmospheric_engine.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Guericke's piston that outpulls a gang of men is in print; the vacuum comes from a pump or gunpowder. Condensing steam under the piston is nobody's idea yet (Papin, 1690). Local: gun founders (brass cylinder, reamed like a cannon); Schemnitz and Idrija mines as users. Elsewhere: The Hague: Huygens (gunpowder cylinder, 1673); Venice: Papin.
